summary: Add inactive canonical SLO breach obligations and ordinary owner-assigned mission source seams, with bounded dispatch and fail-closed readiness.

replay.detail: Explicit claim replay and checkpoint proof rebuild three shared SLO projections from authenticated transition claims. Opening a store creates empty tables only; it adds no history scan or active evaluator.

schema.detail: Add system-only slo.breach-transition and the slo_pending, slo_episode_heads and slo_episode_events tables with three indexes. Older registries retain signed records as unknown; a new build is required to originate them.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules version 16 retains SLO onset, dispatch, owner and recovery fences and conflict witnesses. Redundant receipts of recovered episodes can compact only after seven days under existing reference/envelope guards. Ordinary mission and active-fix history remains retained by its rules.

compatibility.detail: The private source is roll-forward only. Positive dispatch facts are reducer-derived; recovered-before-dispatch uses an intrinsically false receipt so old-registry and partial-import prefixes cannot execute its fix. No public SLO snapshot fields, limits or cursor are added.

downtime.detail: No source callback, new process, deployment or startup backfill is activated. The source change creates empty tables and indexes during normal schema installation.

manual.detail: No live SLO target, owner, threshold or operational setting is changed. Hosted cost qualification and the separate public-contract review precede later activation.

recovery.detail: Durable pending obligations resume after replay; one ordinary mission is linked to each episode. Unknown evidence cannot recover it, and recovery does not complete or cancel an admitted active fix. Failed publication rolls back its transaction and retains pending intake.
